headline: Approved a new noise ordinance, a 90-day license plate reader pilot, and a 20-year solar power credit deal saving about $11 million.
summary: A resolution of no confidence in Mayor Brian A. DePeña passed, with six in favor, three present, and one no. Members also approved a revised noise ordinance, a 90-day license plate reader pilot, and a 20-year solar power credit agreement. Velincia Linette Perez was approved as planning and development director, 7 to 2.
decisions: Approved the resolution of no confidence in Mayor Brian A. DePeña, six in favor, three present, one no.
Tabled item 341-26 on the surveillance technology ordinance (Chapter 9.25) to a later full-council meeting.
Approved a 90-day pilot of SoundThinking PlateRanger license plate readers at no cost to the city, unanimously.
Approved the amended noise ordinance, which police say will make noise rules enforceable.
Approved Velincia Linette Perez as director of the Office of Planning and Development, 7 to 2.
Tabled the home rule petition for creditable service for six firefighters until November 17.
Approved spending the $300 gift from the Estate of Constance M. Gadbois.
Approved spending $43,500 from the BJA FY 2025 Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant.
Approved transferring $2,000 from the Legal Services account to the Claims account.
Approved Cherise J. Davenport's appointment to the Board of Registrars.
Approved a 20-year net metering agreement giving the city a 10% savings, about $11 million over 20 years.
Tabled the zoning change request for 46 Windsor Avenue, with action expected on November 17.
Tabled item 404-26 on a state attorney general complaint against a public official, pending an update from the city attorney.
Approved resident permit parking on multiple streets, with the restriction from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m.
Approved handicap parking additions and removals on several streets, taken as one block.
Approved a child care drop-off zone on the north side of Boswell Street.
Approved a four-way stop at Bruce and Cornish streets and a stop sign on Sunray Street at Highland Avenue.
Withdrew the request for an update on Nunzio DeMarco Park; construction began October 14.
Sent correspondence to the city engineer to review a loading zone at 66 Jackson Street.
Ordered a public hearing on a $10,149,973 bond authorization, to be ratified after the hearing.
discussion: No-confidence resolution: Speakers and members debated whether voters, not the council, should decide confidence in the mayor.
Surveillance cameras: Police and IT described camera counts, outages, and policies, and members asked how camera locations are chosen and who may request video.
Noise ordinance: Members debated whether officers can enforce a noise rule fairly without decibel meters.
Planning director appointment: Members questioned the candidate's lack of a master's degree and planning background, and her salary.
46 Windsor zoning change: Members debated whether the request was spot zoning, and the city attorney's letter said it is.
